title: Nine Days and One Broken Sluice
subtitle: 灾害与防范 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 灾害与防范（灾害防范·灾害类型与应对）
meta: 主题语境：灾害与防范（灾害防范·灾害类型与应对）　|　核心词汇：disaster　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 disaster 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1951 the warden ① reported a disaster that no newspaper in the county would have printed, and he said the reporting was the whole of the night. The ② disaster, meaning the calamity and not the failure, ran nine days and stayed uncounted in the valley; a disaster, he said, is the only thing in a valley that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ disaster in that valley had the same broken sluice at the head of it, and the ④ disaster at the end, meaning the one they kept for the flood year and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever counted twice. A disaster, his deputy said, is nine parts water and one part somebody willing to count; the warden said the counting is the part that fills nine days.

The inspector meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the disaster was the whole of the report, meaning the failure and not the calamity. The ⑥ disaster, meaning the failure and not any of that, is the only thing in a report that everybody cites and nobody prevents; disaster, she said, is either something you report or the only word that means both a calamity and a failure. She said the failure is the part they remember.

By 1959 the ⑦ disaster had become a line in an almanac, and the almanac had become an argument about the broken sluice. The ⑧ disaster of the whole thing, the warden wrote in July, was one valley and nine days of counting; disaster, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to count. She said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ disaster I remember is the one at the end, which was recalled in 1972 and is still described as the quietest in the valley. A ⑩ disaster, the deputy said in 1974, is the only thing that improves by being prevented; every disaster, she said, is a failure that has agreed to look like a calamity. She said the failure was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 灾难；灾害（指山谷里发生的那一场）
B. n. 灾害（指那场灾祸本身，与那次失败相对）
C. 固定搭配：report a disaster 上报一场灾害
D. n. 灾害（指留给洪涝年岁的那一场）
E. n. 灾难；灾祸（抽象总称，指一条山谷的灾情）
F. n. 灾害（指年历上写到、被记下的那一场）
G. n. 惨败；彻底的失败（指报告里被引述的那次）
H. n. 失败（抽象总称，指人人援引却无人预防的那次）

items.q: reported a disaster that no newspaper in the county would have printed
The disaster, meaning the calamity and not the failure
the disaster was the whole of the report
the disaster had become a line in an almanac
The disaster of the whole thing
A disaster, the deputy said in 1974

answers.why: report a disaster 意为“上报一场灾害”，1951 年管理员上报了一场全郡没有一家报纸肯刊载的灾害。
disaster 意为“灾害”，指那场灾祸本身而不是那次失败，它在山谷里历经九天而无人统计。
disaster 意为“灾难、灾害”，指那条山谷里每一场灾害，每一场源头都是同一道破损的水闸。
disaster 意为“灾害”，指留给洪涝年岁的那一场，是唯一有人统计过两次的。
disaster 意为“惨败、彻底的失败”，指报告里被引述的那次，视察员说这次失败就是那份报告的全部。
disaster 意为“失败”，指人人援引却无人预防的那次而不是那场灾祸本身，是报告里人人都援引、却无人预防的东西。
disaster 意为“灾害”，指年历上写到、被记下的那一场，到 1959 年这场灾害成了年历里的一行。
disaster 意为“灾难、灾祸”，管理员七月写道，整件事的灾情是一条山谷和九天的统计。
disaster 意为“灾害”，我记得的是末尾那一场，1972 年被追述，至今仍被说成山谷里最安静的一场。
disaster 为抽象总称，副手 1974 年说，一场灾害是唯一会因为被防住而变得更好的东西。
